research_gaussian_generator.scope: Opt-in for the local noise-* and gl-* research presets only; legacy RAND and default RANDN behavior unchanged.
research_gaussian_generator.algorithm: Two stages of the 32-bit lowbias32 integer permutation. First mix floatBitsToUint(seed) with four distinct additive channel salts, then XOR the packed integer render-target cell coordinates and apply lowbias32 again.
research_gaussian_generator.uniform_mapping: U = ((hash >> 9) + 0.5) / 8388608; a symmetric 23-bit midpoint grid strictly inside (0,1), exactly represented in float32.
research_gaussian_generator.normal_mapping: sqrt(2) * erfinv(2*U-1), retaining the engine approximate odd inverse-erf; its asymmetric endpoint exception is unreachable for this generator.
research_gaussian_generator.temporal_seed: Existing updateRandomSeed() sequence advances once per Euler step when setSeed=false. Cell and Gaussian channel have separate integer keys. No finite sample mean is subtracted.
research_gaussian_generator.coordinate_bound: Packed x and y each use 16 bits, exceeding the 256x128 and 192x192 research grids.
research_gaussian_generator.reason: The legacy float sin/fract hash produced a nonzero point mass at U=0, mapped only to a negative Gaussian tail; the resulting mean favored the negative phase.
research_gaussian_generator.validation_scope: Measured in this browser and WebGL2 implementation with finite samples. Nominal IID errors are descriptive; this does not prove independence at every lag, absence of every possible bias, or identical trajectories across hardware.

GPU_validation.method: Direct WebGL2 RGBA32F noise-only shader draws in this browser, importing both current local randNShader implementations; 100 draws on a 256x128 grid for each initial seed.
GPU_validation.result: The negative mean and zero-uniform endpoint mass measured in all three legacy trials were absent at the tested statistical resolution with the opt-in integer generator. All three corrected first-channel means were within one nominal IID standard error of zero; both channels had near-unit measured variance and no nonfinite values.
